findings.detail: Description of "cancel_transfer_request" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_request_status, cancel_transfer_request · Private data: get_price_quote, cancel_transfer_request · Public sink: create_transfer_request, get_request_status, cancel_transfer_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_request_status, cancel_transfer_request · Private data: get_price_quote, cancel_transfer_request · Public sink: create_transfer_request, get_request_status, cancel_transfer_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_transfer_request" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
